messages.subject: plot blavaan objects (tidySEM) + bf + model comparison
messages.subject_clean: plot blavaan objects (tidySEM) + bf + model comparison
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

as far as I can see, TidySEM only applies to lavaan objects. If this is correct, then I wanted to know:

a) whether some other neat plotting method for the conceptual model exists with effects indicated by bayes factors (instead of p values) for the path coefficients. I know that the esimates for the individual parameters can be plotted via BayesPlot, but I am looking for a plot for the whole model.

b) whether there is any away of converting a blavaan object to a lavaan object to plot the model via TidySEM (or some other way of extracting the information needed from a blavaan object to overwrite a lavaan object for plotting purposes).

In addition, I found it surprisingly difficult to find good tutorials for Blavaan. It would be nice, if someone could point be to some good resource for information on: 1) plotting blavaan objects, 2) Bayes factors for blavaan objects, 3) model comparison for blavaan models.

Thanks!
Niels

messages.subject_clean: plot blavaan objects (tidySEM) + bf + model comparison
messages.body_plain:
Niels

No, so far in blavaan we dont have support for these plots directly. When I do this for publication I have have them made in a graphics program because always found hard to get the automatic plot hao I wanted them.

Given that a lot of the blavaan structure is build on top of lavaan, there are features that work directly. But I dont see a way to switch it directly. You can reach the tidySEM to add features to plot blavaan objects

We are working to improve the tutorials for blavaan in general for a variety of applications and models. About specifics
- I never liked the automatic plots, so I draw the figures I want in other software, like Dia, illustrator, etc
- I dont recommend the use of Bayes Factor in BSEM. Because it is hard to properly define it in models with large number of parameters like SEM. Following the recommendations on the workflow for the proper use of BF (https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.08744 ) it is neccesary to have proper prios, replication test for reliability, and other requirements for it to be thrustworthy. We are intending to do more testing to evaluate its application BSEM, but for now, I dont recommend it
- For model comparison I recommend to use the LOO and WAIC which are probited in the blavCompare() function, accounting for their uncertainty with the respective standard error. The use of these Information criteria leads to a brader model comparison approach focused on the out-of-sample predictive accuracy

Hope this is useful

messages.subject_clean: plot blavaan objects (tidySEM) + bf + model comparison
messages.body_plain:
Niels,

Following up on what Mauricio said:

A blavaan object "inherits" from a lavaan object. So, if "fit" is a blavaan object, we have

> inherits(fit,"lavaan")
[1] TRUE

I have not yet looked at TidySEM, but many methods for lavaan automatically also work for blavaan. But if you really need it to be a lavaan object, it seems that this is also possible:

class(fit) <- "lavaan"

The blavaan plot() command provides access to a variety of plots from the bayesplot package. See the "mcmc_" possibilities here:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/bayesplot/vignettes/plotting-mcmc-draws.html

For example, for a "mcmc_dens" density plot of the first four parameters, you could do

plot(fit, 1:4, "dens")

About tutorials, we plan to add more to the main website in the coming year:

http://ecmerkle.github.io/blavaan/index.html

There is a Laplace approximation to the Bayes factor provided by fitMeasures(), and explicit comparisons between models provided by blavCompare(). And I am not sure that blavaan currently works with the bridgesampling package, though it may become possible in the future. There is also some further detail about model comparison in the blavaan JSS paper here:

https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v085i04

Though part of that paper is outdated, because JAGS was the only sampler when that paper was written, and Stan is now the default.

Hope it helps,
Ed

messages.body_plain:
Dear Mauricio and Ed,

thanks for these responses!

The package is super nice and it is great that blavCompare() reports the WAIC and LOO from the loo package.

I ended up writing some custom functions to fit both a lavaan object and a blavaan object together and then using the blavaan object to
overwrite the estimates of the lavaan object for tidySEM and label the effects with asteriks iff zero is not included in the 95% HDI.
For my purposes this works even if it is not as fancy as adding the blavaan model type to the tidySEM package.

Since the coefficients of the blavaan object and the lavaan object are very similar, the plots of the two models are almost the same.

(The alternative I thought about with the bayes factors was to mark paths with asteriks iff BF > 3 just as e.g. the brms package
permits one to test hypotheses about coefficients after having specified some sensible priors.)

- Niels

messages.body_plain:
Niels

Glad you manage to find a work around it. I would prefer to see the asterisks in function of the HDI instead of the BF, as you describe it here.
Also, a limitation of these figures, are nicer to see but we cant include all the information like the actual credible interval

Here is an FAQ about the use and interpretability of the LOO and WAIC metrics in general
https://avehtari.github.io/modelselection/CV-FAQ.html#1_Where_to_start

take care
